provenance.title: Heteroskedastic Ordered Probit Models with an Artificial Neural Network
affiliations: Missouri University of Science and Technology
provenance.abstract: This paper presents the Ordered Probit model with an ANN (OPANN) for ordinal classification and introduces the Heteroskedastic Ordered Probit model with an ANN (HOPANN). The HOPANN generalizes the OPANN by allowing heteroskedasticity in the variance of the latent ordinal dependent variable. Four predictive experiments are conducted on Amazon software product review star ratings.
key_claims: HOPANN is the first model combining heteroskedastic ordered probit with ANN for ordinal classification
HOPANN and OPANN achieve best/second-best macro F1 scores on all imbalanced datasets
All other models (ANN, SVM, RF, XGB, ordered probit) fail to predict the minority class in imbalanced datasets
RF performs best in accuracy on balanced datasets; XGB is best on PR AUC, MSE, MAE for imbalanced datasets
HOPANN/OPANN are particularly effective for predicting ordinal responses in imbalanced datasets by leveraging the ordered probit probability structure

training_pipeline.curriculum: Hyperparameter search on validation set for Q (hidden nodes) and activation function; final model retrained on full training set
training_pipeline.notes: Adam optimizer confirmed (Kingma 2014 cited). Learning rate, beta1, beta2, batch size, epochs, gradient clipping all unspecified. Early stopping cited (Prechelt 2002) but not formally described. Hardware: T4 GPU, Google Colab.

datasets.name: Amazon Software Product Reviews (Ni et al. 2019) — Experiment 1: 5-star imbalanced
Amazon Software Product Reviews — Experiment 2: Three-class imbalanced
Amazon Software Product Reviews — Experiment 3: Modified three-class imbalanced
Amazon Software Product Reviews — Experiment 4: Modified three-class balanced

reported_results.result: Best or second-best across all imbalanced experiments

baselines: SVM (Support Vector Machine with ordinal extension, scikit-learn)
special_conditions: Time-ordered train/test split to prevent data leakage
Feature standardization fit on training set only; applied to val/test
Asin_verified_share and day dummy variables not standardized
Validation set used for hyperparameter selection (Q, activation function, learning rate)
Final model retrained on full training set after hyperparameter selection

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Adam optimizer default hyperparameters: lr=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8, weight_decay=0
implementation_assumptions.basis: Kingma & Ba (2014) paper defaults; paper does not specify these values

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Q (hidden nodes) is a small integer, likely in range {8, 16, 32, 64} based on dataset size (~6k samples)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Common practice for tabular datasets; paper says Q is hyperparameter-searched

implementation_assumptions.assumption: z_i (variance features for HOPANN) is identical to x_i (same input features)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Paper does not distinguish z_i from x_i explicitly; simplest implementation uses same inputs for both ANN and variance network
alternatives: z_i is a subset of x_i
z_i is a separate engineered feature set

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Variance ANN (heteroskedasticity network) has the same depth (1 hidden layer) and comparable Q as the mean ANN
implementation_assumptions.basis: Paper only explicitly states the mean ANN architecture; symmetric design is common practice
alternatives: single linear layer for variance (z_i gamma)

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Batch size: full-batch or large mini-batch (dataset is ~6k samples, GPU is T4)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Dataset small enough for full-batch; T4 has 16GB VRAM; paper does not state batch size

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Early stopping is applied with a patience-based criterion on validation loss
implementation_assumptions.basis: Prechelt (2002) is cited in the paper; standard practice

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Cutting points c_j are initialized in sorted order (e.g. evenly spaced quantiles of training labels)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Sorted initialization required for ordered probit identifiability; common practice
alternatives: random initialization with sorting constraint enforced via softplus/cumsum
learned free parameters with ordering constraint

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Weight initialization follows PyTorch defaults (Kaiming uniform for ReLU; Xavier uniform for sigmoid/tanh)
implementation_assumptions.basis: PyTorch is the stated framework; default initialization is framework standard

implementation_assumptions.assumption: ANN baseline uses cross-entropy loss (not ordered probit likelihood)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Standard multiclass ANN with softmax implies cross-entropy; paper confirms ANN is a separate baseline

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Total input feature dimension K is approximately 12-19 (12 base features + unspecified number of day binary dummies)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Paper lists 7 named variables; 'Day' expanded to binary dummies; exact count of days not given

ambiguities.description: Paper describes sigma_i = exp(z_i gamma) but also says it is modeled using 'a separate ANN.' It is unclear whether the variance ANN is: (a) a literal ANN replacing the linear z_i*gamma term, or (b) a linear model with exp output.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: sigma_i is produced by a small ANN (hidden layer + exp output) where z_i = x_i
alternatives: sigma_i = exp(z_i * gamma) where gamma is a simple learned vector (no hidden layer)
sigma_i modeled by a separate ANN with different inputs than x_i

ambiguities.description: Batch size is not stated anywhere in the paper.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Mini-batch with batch_size=64 (common default for tabular tasks in PyTorch)

ambiguities.description: The paper says learning rate is searched as a hyperparameter but does not report the final chosen value.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: 1e-3 (Adam default, most common for tabular tasks)

ambiguities.location: Training Pipeline — number of epochs / training steps
ambiguities.description: No epoch count or step count is reported. Early stopping is cited but not described with specific patience or delta thresholds.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Training runs until early stopping triggers (patience=10-20 epochs on validation loss)

ambiguities.location: Implementation Details — feature engineering / day dummies
ambiguities.description: The 'Day' variable is described as a time-fixed effect implemented as binary dummies, but the exact number of dummies is not stated.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Day-of-week dummies (7 binary columns) or a condensed set of time dummies

ambiguities.description: The ordered probit requires c_1 < c_2 < ... < c_{J-1}. The paper does not specify how this ordering constraint is enforced during gradient-based training.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Cumulative sum parameterization: c_j = c_1 + sum_{k=2}^{j} softplus(delta_k) to ensure strict ordering
alternatives: Sorting operation after each gradient step
Free parameters with penalty for ordering violation
